reuse.why: Adds a new range helper and uses it everywhere, but the four inline sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount, which already decides all three cases.

duplication.why: The range arithmetic is now shared, but the `null ? 0 : number ? value : range(...)` dispatch that getScheduledAmount already implements is kept in preview, two schedules/app sites, forecast and the budget template.

placement.why: The new helper sits in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount, which is the right module; the leftover dispatch stays scattered in server modules.

scope.why: Touches only the range rule, its call sites, their comments and a release note.

maintainability.why: Changing the range rule now means editing one function, but anything about missing or approximate amounts still has to be changed in five places, and a maintainer is left with two overlapping helpers (getRangeAmount and getScheduledAmount).

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and budget/schedule-template.ts keep their own dispatch around getRangeAmount instead of calling getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining per-site dispatch copies were already there and are left visibly as they were, not reshaped.

one_place.where: The range rule itself is defined once in getRangeAmount (shared/schedules.ts) and every path that applies it, including getScheduledAmount, now calls it.
